● Create(/home/srjn45/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/fe02b0a7-76c0-4f5a-9d7b-d63b73fe6326/unix_history_essay.md) (ctrl+o to expand)

  I have written a detailed essay on the history of the Unix operating system.

  You can read the full text here: unix_history_essay.md.

  ### Summary of the Essay

  • Origins (1969): Traces Unix back to Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, and others at Bell Labs working on a PDP-7 after the collapse of the Multics project.
  • The C Rewrite (1973): Highlights the revolutionary choice to rewrite the kernel in the newly created C language, granting Unix unmatched portability.
  • Academic Sharing & BSD: Explains how AT&T's regulatory constraints led to source code sharing, which birthed the Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD) and introduced TCP/IP networking.
  • Commercialization & Unix Wars: Details the fragmentation of Unix into proprietary commercial versions (Solaris, AIX, HP-UX) and the ensuing legal battles.
  • The Open Source Era (1980s-1990s): Covers Richard Stallman's GNU Project and Linus Torvalds' release of the Linux kernel in 1991.
  • Modern Legacy: Concludes with how Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS, iOS, Android) dominate current computing alongside the enduring Unix philosophy.
